New Newsletter Categories

With this new issue of the newsletter, I introduce two new categories. The first is Software and Tools. This was inside the EO and RS News category before. But it is worth to be promoted to a main category. The other new category is Beyond EO. Here I want to highlight interesting news from domains other than Earth observation or remote sensing to look beyond our own backyard.

EO and RS News

ESA Survey Regarding Data Access

ESA is seeking insight into how it can improve its Earth observation data access services. If you would like to help, take part in a short survey to help them understand your needs and the challenges you currently face in accessing ESA's EO data.

  • Share your views on ESA data access services

Will Satellites Take Over Your Job?

Okay, the title is click-bait. 😊 But at least image classification can now be done on board a satellite. A team of researchers from Oxford University has developed a system for teaching satellites how to recognize changes in cloud cover from aerial images. The system uses a fast and efficient approach called few-shot learning, which allows the satellite to learn from a few examples. The system could enable faster responses to natural events by reducing the need to transmit and process large amounts of data on Earth.

  • Researchers successfully train a machine learning model in outer space for the first time

  • Fast model inference and training on-board of Satellites

"The Woz", Apple Co-Founder Wants Access to Satellite Data for All

Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, aka "The Woz", has a new space venture: Privateer. The company aims to make satellite data accessible to everyone, not just governments and private companies. Privateer plans to create a marketplace where users can search for and share satellite images at a lower cost, using artificial intelligence and cloud computing. The company also develops a satellite payload device called Pono, which can process data in orbit. Privateer hopes to launch its first Pono device by the end of 2023 and create a ride-sharing economy for space.

  • Privateer wants to create a ‘data ride-sharing economy’ for space

  • Privateer Mediakit 2023

Software and Tools

Python Processing Tool for EnMAP

EnPT Python package automates the pre-processing pipeline for new EnMAP hyperspectral satellite data. The package offers free and open-source features that enable users to convert EnMAP Level-1B data to Level-2A products.

The package has been developed at the German Research Centre for Geosciences Potsdam (GFZ). The version 0.19.4 has recently been released.

  • EnPT - EnMAP Processing Tool (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.8229436)

  • EnPT documentation — EnPT 0.19.4

Open-Source Multi-Sensor Image Co-Registration

Automatically co-register two satellite image datasets at the subpixel scale using an image matching approach that works in the frequency domain. This approach is combined with a multistage workflow to effectively detect false-positives. AROSICS is capable of detecting and correcting both local and global misregistration between two input satellite images at the subpixel scale, which are commonly present in such images.

AROSICS was developed by Daniel Scheffler (German Research Centre of Geosciences) within the context of the GeoMultiSens project.

  • AROSICS: An Automated and Robust Open-Source Image Co-Registration Software for Multi-Sensor Satellite Data (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.8239084)

  • AROSICS documentation — arosics 1.9.2

The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem Jupyter Lab is now open! This means there is a place where you have Sentinel Data at your fingertips, Earth Observation coding tools already installed, and online processing capacity for experimenting.

  • First example notebooks available in Jupyter Lab | Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem

  • Jupyter Notebooks | Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem

Beyond EO

Is Dark Matter Not Necessary to Explain the Universe?

A new study challenges the established gravity models based on Newton and Einstein. By observing the motion of binary stars, a researcher found that the stars behave more in line with the MOND theory, which does not require dark matter to explain the universe. This could have huge implications for astrophysics, cosmology and fundamental physics. However, further confirmation by independent analysis is needed.

  • New Study Provides Evidence for Breakdown of Standard Gravity in Low Acceleration Limit

  • Breakdown of the Newton–Einstein Standard Gravity at Low Acceleration in Internal Dynamics of Wide Binary Stars

  • Modified Newtonian dynamics (MOND) - Wikipedia
